dedupe_keys.name: tale of seven alerts wording of wireless emergency alerts and compliance in reducing mobile data use survey of 898 participants arxiv 2021

description: This study asks how the wording of Wireless Emergency Alerts affects whether smartphone users comply with requests to cut mobile data use during weather disasters, so that civilian channels are not overloaded while first responders and volunteers work. In a between-subjects survey of 898 participants, people received no alert (control) or an alert framed as Basic Information, Altruism, Multimedia, Negative Feedback, Positive Feedback, Reward or Punishment. Basic Information alerts gave the largest reduction in multimedia and video use, and Punishment alerts had the lowest absolute compliance. Producer: Demetrios Lambropoulos, Mohammad Yousefvand and Narayan Mandayam, submitted 1 February 2021. Coverage: an online survey sample, with country not read. Access: free arXiv preprint; only the abstract page was read, and no data release was confirmed. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: self-reported or scenario-based compliance, not measured network load. Simulation uses: the compliance rates by alert framing give behavioural parameters for models of demand reduction during disasters. Related record: the US nationwide alert test of 2023 (case_study-us-nationwide-alert-test-2023).
